=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team  
**Prepared for:** Jay Cho  
**Status:** Preliminary; subject to review of the underlying DD documents (DD-002 to DD-012) and the full SPA draft

---

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

Before the substance, note how the package is presented. The preamble asserts that these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened", and that they are "standard and widely accepted market terms".

- We should **verify internally** whether Wattlebridge principals actually agreed any of this. Nothing in our instructions records an agreed cap, basket or time limit – only price (AUD 24m), structure (100%, debt-free/cash-free) and governing law (NSW). Treat the "agreed" label as a negotiating assertion unless our own principals confirm it.
- Even if a headline **cap number** was discussed commercially, that would not carry the ancillary points the Seller has bolted on (fundamental warranties inside the cap, all-Claims sweep, "discoverable" buyer-knowledge exclusion, general data-room disclosure). Those are drafting positions, not commercial bargain.
- The "market" characterisation is self-serving. For an Australian mid-market SaaS share sale, a 20% general cap is at the **low end**; what is genuinely market is that fundamental, title and tax matters sit **outside** the general cap at 100% of price, and that specific indemnities for known issues sit outside the warranty regime altogether. The draft departs from that on every count.

The Disclosure Letter is also internally revealing: paragraph 11 expressly says it contains "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval" and that the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts" itself. The Seller is deliberately leaving the risk assessment to us. We should.

---

## 2. Material issues – by priority

### A. Deal-critical (condition / completion mechanics)

**A1. Riverlark Bank facility (~AUD 3.2m) – "release following Completion"**  
The baseline is debt-free/cash-free. A AUD 3.2m facility that remains outstanding at Completion, with security undischarged, is the single biggest departure from the agreed deal. Additional problems: DD-003 cl 8.1 is a change-of-control clause – completing without the bank's consent or payout will put the Company in default on day one, with security over its assets enforceable against *our* company. "Release to be provided following Completion" means we rely on the Seller's post-Completion goodwill and the bank's cooperation, with no leverage.

*Push back:* Repayment at Completion from the purchase price via the funds flow, against a bank payout letter stating the exact payout figure, a deed of release and PPSR discharge (or undertaking to discharge within a fixed short period, with Seller indemnity for failure) delivered **at** Completion. Check whether the bank also holds security over the **shares** or a Harbourglass guarantee – if so, that is a title issue too (see D1).

**A2. Bluefen change-of-control consent (~30% of revenue)**  
Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue. DD-002 cl 11.2 requires consent and cl 11.3 attaches conditions. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the conditions are satisfied. The Seller proposes "reasonable endeavours" and deems the condition satisfied on "delivery of the counterparty's written consent" – which could be a conditional or qualified consent, or one whose cl 11.3 conditions remain unmet.

*Push back:*
- Condition precedent: **unconditional** written consent from Bluefen, in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), **plus** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, delivered before Completion.
- Seller obligation: "all reasonable endeavours" (or "best endeavours"), with Buyer entitled to participate in Bluefen discussions, and a long-stop date with Buyer termination right.
- Specific warranty that Bluefen has not indicated any intention to terminate, reduce scope or renegotiate pricing.
- Consider commercial protection if the consent is obtained but Bluefen churns within, say, 12 months: price retention/escrow, or a revenue-based deferred consideration component.

**A3. Ironquay IP – ownership of SOW3 Project Materials**  
DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment. On the documents, the Company may **not currently own** the SOW3 deliverables. For a SaaS target, if those materials are in the product, that is a core-asset defect, not a payables issue. The Seller's proposal to confine the indemnity to the SOW3 **payment** misdescribes the risk: the exposure is loss of IP, infringement claims, licence-back costs and re-development, not AUD 180k.

*Push back:*
- Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** a confirmatory deed of assignment (and moral-rights consents) from Ironquay and any individual developers.
- Specific indemnity covering all loss arising from any failure of title to Ironquay-developed materials (SOW1–3, not just SOW3), sitting outside cap, basket and general time limits.
- Unqualified IP ownership warranty covering all product code and documentation, with a cap at 100% of price.
- DD: confirm what SOW3 materials are and whether they are in production.

**A4. Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000, DD-005) – excluded from funds flow**  
These are triggered by Completion and (via the continued-employment conditions) may straddle Completion. They are a transaction cost of the Seller. "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised" leaves two problems: (i) if the Company is the employer, the Company pays unless the SPA says otherwise – i.e. we pay; (ii) on-costs are ignored. Superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) take the gross exposure to roughly AUD 490–500k.

*Push back:* Define "Transaction Bonuses" (including super, payroll tax, PAYG withholding and any associated on-costs) as Debt / Seller transaction costs and either deduct from the price or pay from Seller proceeds through the funds flow; Seller indemnity for any shortfall; confirm in the employment schedule which obligations survive and who funds the "continued employment" retention tail.

**A5. Debt-free/cash-free definitions generally**  
Items A1, A4 and C2 below each show the Seller treating known liabilities as outside "Debt". Audit the Debt / Debt-like definition to capture: Riverlark principal, interest and break costs; Transaction Bonuses and on-costs; accrued but unpaid tax; deferred revenue (depending on the working-capital mechanic); the Ironquay AUD 180k; and any pre-paid or committed supplier renewals not in normal working capital.

### B. Liability regime

**B1. General cap – 20% / AUD 4.8m**  
Low for this market and this risk profile (customer concentration, unresolved IP title, open privacy incident). Our opening should be materially higher (50% is a defensible ask; we should expect to land in the 30–50% range). Alternatively, if the Seller insists on a low cap, explore W&I insurance with the Seller contributing to premium, and/or a retention/escrow.

**B2. Fundamental / title warranties inside the general cap and 18-month limit**  
Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery for not owning the shares we are paying AUD 24m for. Capacity, authority, title (shares and the Company's ownership of its subsidiaries/IP) should be at **100% of price**, with a limitation period of at least 6–7 years or none.

**B3. Tax and IP "under the general regime"**  
Reject. Tax warranties and a standalone tax indemnity should be at 100% of price with a period matching ATO amendment periods plus a margin (commonly 7 years from Completion). Given this is a SaaS business, IP ownership/non-infringement warranties warrant an elevated cap (we would propose 100%; fallback 50%).

**B4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13) and "limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**  
This is the most dangerous drafting in the package because it operates silently: it sweeps the specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax, leakage/price-adjustment claims, pre-Completion covenants, restraint breaches and even the Seller's Completion obligations into a 20% cap, a AUD 250k basket and an 18-month window.

*Push back:* Reverse the default. Caps, thresholds and time limits apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and nothing else unless expressly stated. Express carve-outs for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; fundamental/title warranties; tax; specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark, Transaction Bonuses); leakage and completion accounts adjustments; Seller covenants and Completion obligations. Note that non-reliance wording cannot exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 ACL in any event; we should ensure the clause does not purport to, and that fraud is expressly preserved.

**B5. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**  
De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%) and basket AUD 250k (~1%) are within range, but the basket should be **tipping** (recover from the first dollar once exceeded), not deductible. Thresholds should not apply to the carve-out categories in B4. Add aggregation language so a series of related claims (cf. the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals) counts together.

**B6. Time limits**  
18 months for general warranties is acceptable, but push for 24 months (two audit cycles). Tax: 7 years. Fundamental: 6+ years. Add a reasonable window after notification to issue proceedings (6–9 months) rather than a hard notification-only bar.

**B7. Seller covenant strength**  
Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd is a Pty Ltd vendor. If it is an SPV or will distribute proceeds, the cap is theoretical. Require a parent/shareholder guarantee or an escrow/retention (we would propose 10–15% of price for 18–24 months, higher if Bluefen consent or the DD-006 investigation remains open at Completion).

### C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**C1. General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1, 1.2)**  
Reject. The standard should be matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Public searches should be confined to a scheduled list of searches actually run (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court registers) at specified dates. "Discoverable from public records" is open-ended.

**C2. Buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3) – "knowledge… including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records"**  
Reject. "Discoverable" is close to a complete exclusion of the warranty package. If any knowledge qualification is conceded at all, confine it to **actual** knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals of a matter **fairly disclosed** in the DL, and include the standard clause that the Buyer's investigations do not otherwise reduce or extinguish any Claim.

**C3. Stale cut-off**  
The DL speaks as at 22 September 2026; it is now November. Require an updated DL at signing and a bring-down at Completion, with the Completion update **not** permitted to qualify the warranties (or, if it does, a Buyer termination right and/or price adjustment for matters disclosed). Ask why paragraph 1.3 is missing from the DL numbering.

**C4. DL 1.4 reservation**  
Not objectionable in itself, but it signals that the Seller is deliberately not conceding that Bluefen consent, Riverlark release, Ironquay payment, privacy notification or Mossvale consent are "legally required". We should not rely on the DL for those conclusions; our own reading of DD-002/003/004/006/009 governs.

### D. Specific disclosed matters

**D1. Title (DD-012 share register)**  
A share register is prima facie evidence only; the Seller's own disclosure flags that the Buyer "has not completed its own verification". We should: run ASIC and PPSR searches against both Harbourglass and the Company (including any security over the shares connected with Riverlark); obtain share certificates, executed transfers, board resolutions approving the transfer and registration; and warrant no options, convertibles, pre-emptive rights or shareholder agreements. Title warranty unqualified and uncapped (B2).

**D2. DD-006 export/privacy incident**  
The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" – that is characterisation, not disclosure. ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps were sent to an unintended external address. Under the Privacy Act 1988 NDB scheme the Company must assess within 30 days whether this is an eligible data breach (likely serious harm test) and notify the OAIC and affected individuals if so; the September incident date means that clock has likely already run. There may also be contractual notification obligations to customers (Bluefen in particular – an open incident could jeopardise the consent in A2) and, if any data subjects are in the EU/UK, GDPR exposure. Civil penalties post-2022 amendments are substantial.

*Push back:* Seller to complete the assessment and any required notifications before Completion and share the findings; specific indemnity for all loss (regulatory, customer claims, remediation, notification costs) arising from the incident, outside cap/basket/time limits; warranty of no other security incidents; Buyer control of the matter post-Completion with Seller cooperation.

**D3. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110k)**  
The DL itself invites us to "read together" DD-008 and DD-011 – three identical amounts split across documents is a pattern we should examine, not accept as "ordinary course". Questions: are these committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit (price/working-capital issue)? Terminable? Is Sandbar related to the Seller? Ensure the aggregation language in B5 captures them and that any committed-but-unaccrued amounts are treated as Debt-like or excluded from normal working capital.

**D4. Office lease (DD-007)**  
The Seller says "notification", not "consent". Many commercial leases deem a change in control of a corporate tenant to be an assignment requiring landlord consent. We should read the lease ourselves; if it is consent, add to the conditions list; if notice only, make it a Completion deliverable with a warranty that no further consent is required.

**D5. Mossvale (DD-009)**  
The Seller's wording ("does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold") is carefully chosen. Check for change-of-control, "deemed assignment" or termination-for-convenience provisions. More broadly, obtain a warranty listing **every** material contract with a change-of-control or anti-assignment right, with Bluefen and Mossvale as the only exceptions identified, and a specific indemnity for any loss from an undisclosed one.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Recommended Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay at Completion from price via funds flow; payout letter, release and PPSR discharge at Completion; CP if bank consent needed |
| 2 | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on any written consent | CP: unconditional consent in Buyer-approved form + cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; all-reasonable-endeavours; long-stop; churn protection (escrow/deferred) |
| 3 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Completion deliverable: payment evidence + confirmatory assignment; broad IP title indemnity outside caps; 100% IP warranty cap |
| 4 | Completion bonuses AUD 420k | "Matter for Seller", not in funds flow | Treat as Debt/Seller cost incl. super and payroll tax (~AUD 495k); deduct or pay from Seller proceeds; indemnity |
| 5 | General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Open at 50%; consider W&I and/or escrow; escrow/guarantee regardless given Pty Ltd vendor |
| 6 | Fundamental/title/tax/IP | Inside general cap and 18 months | 100% of price; title/fundamental 6+ years; tax 7 years |
| 7 | Limitations apply to "all Claims" | Default sweep-in | Reverse default; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, leakage/adjustments, covenants |
| 8 | Basket | Deductible, AUD 250k | Tipping basket; aggregation of related claims; not applicable to carve-outs |
| 9 | Disclosure | General data room + public records | Fair-disclosure standard; scheduled searches only; updated DL at signing; no qualifying bring-down |
| 10 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Includes "discoverable" matters | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters |
| 11 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | NDB assessment/notifications pre-Completion; specific uncapped indemnity; Buyer control |
| 12 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Investigate timing, relatedness and terminability; aggregate for thresholds; Debt-like if committed pre-Completion |
| 13 | Title | Share register only | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; certificates, transfers, approvals; unqualified uncapped title warranty |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Notice only / no consent | Read source documents; warranty scheduling all CoC rights; indemnity for undisclosed ones |
| 15 | "FINAL" framing | Not to be re-opened | Confirm with Wattlebridge principals what, if anything, was actually agreed; treat the rest as open |

**Suggested immediate next steps**

1. Confirm internally whether any principal-level agreement exists on cap/basket/time limits.
2. Pull and review DD-002, 003, 004, 006, 007, 009 and 012 against the Seller's characterisations – the DL repeatedly signals that the Seller's descriptions are narrower than the documents.
3. Run ASIC and PPSR searches on Harbourglass and Paperbark now, particularly for Riverlark security over the shares.
4. Issue a mark-up leading with items 1–4 (deal mechanics) as non-negotiable, then the liability regime (5–8), then disclosure/knowledge (9–10).

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up table or draft the specific indemnity and carve-out language if useful.

Alternatively, if the Seller insists on a low cap, explore W&I insurance with the Seller contributing to premium, and/or a retention/escrow.

**B2. Fundamental / title warranties inside the general cap and 18-month limit**  
Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery for not owning the shares we are paying AUD 24m for. Capacity, authority, title (shares and the Company's ownership of its subsidiaries/IP) should be at **100% of price**, with a limitation period of at least 6–7 years or none.

**B3. Tax and IP "under the general regime"**  
Reject. Tax warranties and a standalone tax indemnity should be at 100% of price with a period matching ATO amendment periods plus a margin (commonly 7 years from Completion). Given this is a SaaS business, IP ownership/non-infringement warranties warrant an elevated cap (we would propose 100%; fallback 50%).

**B4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13) and "limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**  
This is the most dangerous drafting in the package because it operates silently: it sweeps the specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax, leakage/price-adjustment claims, pre-Completion covenants, restraint breaches and even the Seller's Completion obligations into a 20% cap, a AUD 250k basket and an 18-month window.

*Push back:* Reverse the default. Caps, thresholds and time limits apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and nothing else unless expressly stated. Express carve-outs for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; fundamental/title warranties; tax; specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark, Transaction Bonuses); leakage and completion accounts adjustments; Seller covenants and Completion obligations. Note that non-reliance wording cannot exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 ACL in any event; we should ensure the clause does not purport to, and that fraud is expressly preserved.

**B5. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**  
De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%) and basket AUD 250k (~1%) are within range, but the basket should be **tipping** (recover from the first dollar once exceeded), not deductible. Thresholds should not apply to the carve-out categories in B4. Add aggregation language so a series of related claims (cf. the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals) counts together.

**B6. Time limits**  
18 months for general warranties is acceptable, but push for 24 months (two audit cycles). Tax: 7 years. Fundamental: 6+ years. Add a reasonable window after notification to issue proceedings (6–9 months) rather than a hard notification-only bar.

**B7. Seller covenant strength**  
Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd is a Pty Ltd vendor. If it is an SPV or will distribute proceeds, the cap is theoretical. Require a parent/shareholder guarantee or an escrow/retention (we would propose 10–15% of price for 18–24 months, higher if Bluefen consent or the DD-006 investigation remains open at Completion).

### C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**C1. General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1, 1.2)**  
Reject. The standard should be matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Public searches should be confined to a scheduled list of searches actually run (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court registers) at specified dates. "Discoverable from public records" is open-ended.

**C2. Buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3) – "knowledge… including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records"**  
Reject. "Discoverable" is close to a complete exclusion of the warranty package. If any knowledge qualification is conceded at all, confine it to **actual** knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals of a matter **fairly disclosed** in the DL, and include the standard clause that the Buyer's investigations do not otherwise reduce or extinguish any Claim.

**C3. Stale cut-off**  
The DL speaks as at 22 September 2026; it is now November. Require an updated DL at signing and a bring-down at Completion, with the Completion update **not** permitted to qualify the warranties (or, if it does, a Buyer termination right and/or price adjustment for matters disclosed). Ask why paragraph 1.3 is missing from the DL numbering.

**C4. DL 1.4 reservation**  
Not objectionable in itself, but it signals that the Seller is deliberately not conceding that Bluefen consent, Riverlark release, Ironquay payment, privacy notification or Mossvale consent are "legally required". We should not rely on the DL for those conclusions; our own reading of DD-002/003/004/006/009 governs.

### D. Specific disclosed matters

**D1. Title (DD-012 share register)**  
A share register is prima facie evidence only; the Seller's own disclosure flags that the Buyer "has not completed its own verification". We should: run ASIC and PPSR searches against both Harbourglass and the Company (including any security over the shares connected with Riverlark); obtain share certificates, executed transfers, board resolutions approving the transfer and registration; and warrant no options, convertibles, pre-emptive rights or shareholder agreements. Title warranty unqualified and uncapped (B2).

**D2. DD-006 export/privacy incident**  
The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" – that is characterisation, not disclosure. ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps were sent to an unintended external address. Under the Privacy Act 1988 NDB scheme the Company must assess within 30 days whether this is an eligible data breach (likely serious harm test) and notify the OAIC and affected individuals if so; the September incident date means that clock has likely already run. There may also be contractual notification obligations to customers (Bluefen in particular – an open incident could jeopardise the consent in A2) and, if any data subjects are in the EU/UK, GDPR exposure. Civil penalties post-2022 amendments are substantial.

*Push back:* Seller to complete the assessment and any required notifications before Completion and share the findings; specific indemnity for all loss (regulatory, customer claims, remediation, notification costs) arising from the incident, outside cap/basket/time limits; warranty of no other security incidents; Buyer control of the matter post-Completion with Seller cooperation.

**D3. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110k)**  
The DL itself invites us to "read together" DD-008 and DD-011 – three identical amounts split across documents is a pattern we should examine, not accept as "ordinary course". Questions: are these committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit (price/working-capital issue)? Terminable? Is Sandbar related to the Seller? Ensure the aggregation language in B5 captures them and that any committed-but-unaccrued amounts are treated as Debt-like or excluded from normal working capital.

**D4. Office lease (DD-007)**  
The Seller says "notification", not "consent". Many commercial leases deem a change in control of a corporate tenant to be an assignment requiring landlord consent. We should read the lease ourselves; if it is consent, add to the conditions list; if notice only, make it a Completion deliverable with a warranty that no further consent is required.

**D5. Mossvale (DD-009)**  
The Seller's wording ("does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold") is carefully chosen. Check for change-of-control, "deemed assignment" or termination-for-convenience provisions. More broadly, obtain a warranty listing **every** material contract with a change-of-control or anti-assignment right, with Bluefen and Mossvale as the only exceptions identified, and a specific indemnity for any loss from an undisclosed one.
